items.title: 9.8.2 Salts of strong acids and weak bases

blocks.text: For salts derived from strong acids and weak bases, such as ammonium chloride, the conjugate base of the strong acid (Cl-) does not react with water, while the conjugate acid of the weak base (NH4+ from NH3) reacts with water to produce H3O+ ions, making the solution acidic. NH4Cl(s) gives NH4+(aq) + Cl-(aq); NH4+ is the conjugate acid of the weak base NH3 and reacts with water, NH4+(aq) + H2O(l) gives NH3 + H3O+(aq); Cl- is the conjugate base of HCl and does not affect the pH. The solution is acidic because of the NH4+ ion.

blocks.prompt: Explain with an equation why a solution of ammonium nitrate turns blue litmus red.
blocks.explanation: NH4NO3 gives NH4+ and NO3-. Nitrate, from the strong acid HNO3, does not react, but NH4+, the conjugate acid of the weak base ammonia, donates a proton to water: NH4+ + H2O gives NH3 + H3O+. The H3O+ makes the solution acidic, so blue litmus turns red.

items: Strong acid + weak base salt (NH4Cl): NH4+ hydrolyses to NH3 + H3O+, Cl- does not; the solution is acidic.
